multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots

subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts

concepts.why: The patient has violaceous cutaneous lesions consistent with leukemia cutis and a high percentage of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid analysis.
The patient has a high white blood cell count, a high percentage of atypical cells/blasts, and a significant red blood cell count, which are consistent with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
The patient has severe flaccid quadriparesis and nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots, which are consistent with Neurolymphomatosis.
The patient has severe flaccid quadriparesis and nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots, which are consistent with CNS Lymphoma.
The patient has severe flaccid quadriparesis and reduced muscle stretch reflexes, which are consistent with Guillain-Barre Syndrome.
The patient has urinary retention and nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots, which are consistent with Spinal Cord Compression.

rationales.F01: Subacute progressive symmetric lower extremity weakness is more typical of leukemia or neurolymphomatosis than Guillain-Barre Syndrome or spinal cord compression.
rationales.F04: Severe flaccid quadriparesis is a strong indicator of leukemia or neurolymphomatosis.
rationales.F06: Violaceous cutaneous lesions are a strong indicator of leukemia.
rationales.F09: Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots is more typical of leukemia or neurolymphomatosis than Guillain-Barre Syndrome or spinal cord compression.
rationales.F11: Cell differential showing 98% atypical cells/blasts is a strong indicator of leukemia.
